text:
rachel: flipped tenant `nova-labs` to v2-prefer for a tiny canary (4%) at 08:10 PT. PM flagged a sudden v1 token bump in the routes dashboard. anyone on routing/metrics?

opsbot: config-change: tenant=nova-labs v2_prefer=true @2025-08-21T15:10:00Z

anya: quick check: router traces show chosen_route=v2 for sampled reqs, but billing logs attribute some tokens to meter_key=v1 for ~90s after the flip. looks like billing memo cache lag.

marco: confirm: billing caches tenant->meter_key for 5m. when we toggle routes, router is immediate but billing still uses cached mapping until invalidation.

rachel: two immediate asks: 1) can we set pin.ttl=0 for nova-labs to avoid sticky fallbacks? 2) can we lower billing memo ttl for canary tenants?

billing-bot: applied: pin.ttl(nova-labs)=0 by rachel @2025-08-21T15:12:10Z

marco: i'll push a small billing patch to accept a pubsub invalidation on `tenant-routing:update`. low-risk; will stage now.

anya: UX quick win: show a toast when toggling route flags: "Billing attribution may lag ~2m due to caching" and add chart toggle "show by chosen route / show by billing key" so PMs don't misread spikes.

rachel: perfect. also can analytics surface `last_billing_sync_age` per tenant so we can suppress quota alerts during flips?

marco: yes we can emit last_meter_update and analytics can compute sync_age. i'll include the invalidation event so sync_age drops quickly.

anya: follow-ups: marco -> pubsub invalidation PR + prod rollout; anya -> toast copy + chart toggle mock; rachel -> update canary runbook to set pin.ttl=0 and run billing-cache-short TTL.

rachel: metrics realigned after ~70s. filing RFC and linking PRs/mocks. closing once RFC posted. :thumbsup:
